title: WO-7 (closed): Add 2000 ms controller watchdog
text: Past work order. Added WATCHDOG_MS 2000 and check_watchdog to stop runaway delivery when the controller hangs (H-5). Lesson: any change to timing constants needs SR-5 re-verified.

title: Clinical safety review, Oct 28 (transcript summary)
text: Clinical lead: never raise the 10 U single-bolus cap. Large meals should use an extended or dual-wave bolus delivered over time. Typing errors (decimal slips) are the top real-world overdose cause in pump incident reports.

title: #pump-firmware Slack thread
text: Product asked for bigger meal boluses for adult users with high insulin needs (carb ratio 5). Firmware lead: OK only if per-hour delivery stays within the max bolus rate and the daily cap of 60 U still applies.

title: Email from regulatory affairs: IEC 62304 evidence
text: For the next submission every software change to the bolus path needs: hazard analysis update (ISO 14971), traceability from requirement to test, and verification evidence. Simulation evidence from a validated patient model (UVA/Padova) is accepted as supporting evidence.

title: Open finding: insulin-sensitive patients and decimal slips
text: World model on main: for insulin-sensitive patients (carb ratio 16 to 22) a 10x typo stays under the 10 U cap and causes severe hypoglycemia. Proposed SR-6: cap a single bolus relative to the patient's configured carb ratio.

title: demo/pump/pump.c dependency map
text: request_bolus checks MAX_BOLUS_U (SR-1), MIN_BG_FOR_BOLUS (SR-3) and MAX_DAILY_U via delivered_today_u (SR-2). check_occlusion uses OCCLUSION_KPA (SR-4). check_watchdog uses WATCHDOG_MS (SR-5). Any edit to pump.h constants affects every requirement that reads it.

title: Flight controls safety review, Nov 3 (summary)
text: AoA stall protection (Boeing Flight Controls). The 5.5 deg AoA disagree monitor AOA_DISAGREE_DEG is the certified value from the 737 MAX return-to-service AD 2020-24-02; changing it re-opens the system safety assessment (ARP4761) and SR-2/SR-3. Crew alerts must be separate from protection logic: an alert threshold must never switch stall protection off.

title: fcc.h: AoA monitor shared by SR-2 and SR-3
text: AOA_DISAGREE_DEG decides both when protection is inhibited (SR-2, H-1) and when it must stay available (SR-3, H-2). In a sideslip near the stall the two fuselage AoA vanes read about 5 deg apart. A new AoA disagree alert needs its own constant, e.g. AOA_ALERT_DEG, and the fcc_aoa_disagree() interface in fcc.h.

title: WO-31 (closed): Inhibit stall protection on AoA disagree (post-MCAS)
text: Past work order. Protection now votes both AoA vanes and does nothing when they disagree by more than 5.5 deg, has 2.5 deg authority and never latches, as in the 737 MAX fix. Open item: hazard H-3, the crew gets no AOA DISAGREE alert yet.

title: FCS-2231 incident ticket: AoA sensor disagree in a sideslip approach
text: In-service report (synthetic). Crosswind approach with about 4 deg of sideslip: left and right AoA vanes read 5.3 deg apart for 9 s. Stall protection stayed available because the split stayed under the certified 5.5 deg inhibit. Root cause: aerodynamic sideslip effect on fuselage-mounted vanes, not a vane failure. Corrective action: no alert or monitor threshold below 5.5 deg may inhibit stall protection (SR-3, H-2).

title: DER review comment on the AoA monitor change (SOI-2 desk review)
text: Designated Engineering Representative (synthetic): every change to the stall protection function must trace to its FHA failure condition (H-1, H-2), to a DAL A high-level requirement and to a requirements-based test with normal-range and robustness cases (DO-178C A-6). Test the vane split at 5.0, 5.3 and 5.6 deg. A tool that approves code without independent review of its output needs DO-330 qualification.

title: #fcc-software Slack thread: AOA DISAGREE alert
text: Pilot representative (synthetic): the AOA DISAGREE alert must be standard on every display, not an option. Software lead: fine as an advisory-only crew alert at 5 deg with its own constant; the 5.5 deg protection inhibit stays exactly as certified.

title: Email from certification liaison: hardware vs software evidence
text: Certification liaison (synthetic): the dual-channel AoA voter FPGA is airborne electronic hardware and needs DO-254 design assurance at DAL A; the flight control software follows DO-178C. Keep the hardware and software trace data separate, and record every software change against its FHA failure condition for the next Stage of Involvement audit.
